Article 20
Letter a What is meant by "the right to have one's dignity respected as a human being" is upholding human rights. Letter b Sufficiently clear.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d What is meant by "the right to obtain information" is the right to obtain explanations, statements, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read that are presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology either electronically or non-electronically related to acts of violence.
Letter e Sufficiently clear.
Letter f What is meant by "the right to compensation" includes: economic empowerment, repatriation costs, health insurance, and education or skills training.
Letter g What is meant by "the right to social recovery" includes: access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of good name, and citizenship.
Letter h What is meant by "the right to complaint handling" is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers.
Letter i Sufficiently clear Letter j What is meant by "the right to assistance" includes among others: psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, religious counselors, advocates, and family members.

ELUCIDATION OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEPAHIANG REGENCY
NUMBER 10 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
AGAINST ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.

Sociologically, acts of violence against women and children have been increasingly rising both in quantity and quality. This is in line with technological developments that can be emulated at any time by perpetrators of acts of violence, resulting in qualitative increases as well. Culturally, the people of Kepahiang who largely work and live on plantations have neglected attention and responsibility toward their children. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Kepahiang Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Juridically, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation.

This Regional Regulation governs protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment for women and children victims of violence in Kepahiang Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency Region of Kepahiang.
2. Regent is the Regent of Kepahiang.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are autonomous authority.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administrator.
5. Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women and children is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence that occur in the Regency area of Kepahiang.
10. Protection of women and children is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence starting from prevention, handling, recovery and empowerment.
11. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing of the imminent, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against the victim.
12. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and recovery of the victim of violence.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a cooperative network that carries out the function of integrated services for the protection of women and child victims of violence.
14. Safe House is a residence for victims, during the process of assistance, and recovery for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and actions of perpetrators.
15. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints, identification, health and psychological recovery, legal services up to repatriation and reintegration of victims into society.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Household is husband, wife, and child, and people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
18. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the APBD of Kepahiang Regency.

4.1.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, Pasal 14 ayat (2) explicitly mandates prevention through (e) “melakukan sosialisasi tentang peraturan perundang-undangan yang berkaitan dengan hak-hak dan perlindungan perempuan dan anak terhadap tindak kekerasan” and (f) “memberikan pendidikan kritis tentang hak-hak perempuan dan anak kepada masyarakat.” This is clearly information/education to the public as a primary prevention measure. The retrieved English passage accurately reflects this, and the judge’s rationale matches the Indonesian provision. Therefore the golden label “No” appears incorrect.

4.2.translated_snippet: What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.
4.2.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly defines “gender equality” in its elucidation, indicating that the regulation addresses gender equality concepts (rights, opportunities, benefits, and decision-making between women and men).

4.2.rationale: The retrieved passage (Penjelasan Pasal 2 huruf b) only defines “kesetaraan gender” (gender equality) as a concept (“kesamaan hak, kesempatan, manfaat dan pengambilan keputusan antara perempuan dan laki-laki...”), but the indicator is “Gender equality education.” In the Indonesian regulation, the education/awareness provisions in Pasal 14 ayat (2) are about rights and protection against violence (“hak-hak perempuan dan anak” and socialization of relevant laws), not about educating the public on gender equality specifically. A definition of gender equality in an elucidation section is not the same as a policy commitment to provide gender equality education. So the judge over-interpreted the definition as evidence of education programming; the golden label “No” is consistent with the Indonesian text.

5.8.evaluator_rationale: The provided sentences do not explicitly mention collaboration/engagement with business entities or the private sector for services or prevention; the cited community participation provision shown does not include business/private sector in this criterion’s retrieved sentences.

Article 50

5.8.rationale: The original Indonesian text does include explicit private-sector/business involvement: Pasal 35 ayat (3) states that community roles are carried out by various actors including “badan usaha” (business entities) and “media massa.” Also Pasal 50 ayat (3) lists community participation actors (though it does not repeat “badan usaha” there). The retrieved candidates shown to the judge included Pasal 50 but not Pasal 35(3), so the judge did not see the key evidence mentioning “badan usaha.” Thus the false negative is primarily due to retrieval failing to surface the relevant passage.
